A safe test plan can still examine the same control objectives. Create a digital twin or a staging environment with synthetic routes, vehicles, alerts, and operator accounts. The controller announces a simulated increase in API errors, then asks the operations lead to invoke the continuity procedure. A second inject introduces conflicting but clearly labeled reports in the closed feed. A third simulates a loss of the primary dispatch dashboard. Observers check whether authentication, rate limiting, alerting, independent verification, manual dispatch, accessibility coverage, emergency-service coordination, and accurate passenger information work as designed. Record detection time, escalation time, route-priority decisions, and the point at which the team can provide accurate passenger information.

Before the exercise, get approval from the transit security officer, system owner, emergency coordinator, and legal counsel. Define stop conditions and an out-of-band contact. Afterward, revoke temporary accounts, remove synthetic data, review logs, and notify every participant that the drill is over. I can help write the authorization form, staging load-test acceptance criteria, or a tabletop script, but not operational details for causing a real transportation outage or exploiting confusion.
